THIS IS VERY DANGEROUS FOR ANTHROPIC, $ANT.

Morgan Stanley, the bank responsible for supporting Anthropic's stock after the IPO, has already used up its full buying option, just 1 day after listing, per Reuters 

1. It had 30 days to use it.

2. It bought all 147 million extra shares directly from Anthropic at the $83 IPO price.

3. That lifted Anthropic's total IPO raise to about $93.5 billion.

4. But now, the bank can no longer buy shares in the market if the stock falls below $83.

And the stock is already close to falling below its $83 IPO price.

• Down 23% from its $115 peak
• $470 billion wiped out in 2 days
• Friday low: $83.20, just 20 cents above the IPO price

Berenberg says the banks have given up their remaining stabilisation option already after 1 day.

Now $ANT has no safety net.

Just six months ago it was a two-company race between OpenAI and Anthropic.

I expect this race to keep going with many more companies in it. I also expect we'll soon see breakthroughs in math and biology from companies other than OpenAI and Anthropic. With that much competition, scientific breakthroughs are going to accelerate too.

Good to see CBC willing to run a critical piece on Brookfield’s role in Madrid’s housing crunch—tenants in former public housing accusing the firm of letting leases expire and pricing them out

It’s long past time they applied the same scrutiny to Mark Carney’s ongoing Brookfield ties and conflicts as Prime Minister

A short list:  
• Ethics screen covering only a fraction of Brookfield’s ~2,000 entities while he retains carried interest and long-dated options in transition funds that can still pay out.  
• $2B heat-pump incentives while Brookfield owns Enercare (and related HVAC/heat-pump businesses); PSP just bought half of Enercare from them.  
• Transition funds he co-headed structured through Bermuda; government now buying CO2-removal credits.  
• Timeline correlations between his PM travels and major Brookfield deals (Qatar AI, French data centres, Australian storage, U.S. Westinghouse financing, etc.).  
• Telesat $2.3B contract involving a personal friend, triggering a new ethics screen.  
• Past indigenous-rights and environmental complaints against Brookfield operations in Brazil, Ontario, and elsewhere during his tenure.

CBC has covered bits and pieces of this in isolation. A single, hard look at the full pattern of residual financial interests, policy overlaps, and incomplete screens is very much in order @brodiefenlon

Covid and my highly concentrated position in Bajaj finance taught me a lesson I’ve not forgotten since. If you have a habit of over allocating to any idea or theme it’s a matter of time before the market finds you and kills you. It’s a certainty. 

What’s more painful is that your thesis may be right and the stock eventually bounces back but the over allocation forces your hand. 

So the lesson I learnt is actually as old as the hills. It  is to never be in a position where the market can force your hand. 

Whether you own Gold, silver or global AI - if you didn’t over allocate not only are you living to fight another day but you have a fair chance to participate in the bounce back.
